data.description:
## Problem
The completion verifier's step budget routinely exhausts on legitimate validation work, failing criteria as "unmet" that are merely unproven-within-budget. Two epic closes hit this in one day (fb8a: request_limit=24 exhausted, 2 false unmets; the pony epic: repeated exhaustion across re-verifies, 5 then 1 false unmets), and the pressure drives operators/agents toward attestation-laundering.

## Design intent (operator-stated, canonical)
The ONLY goal of the budget floor is to prevent runaway tool use that spends tokens without delivering a result. For VALID tool use the floor must be GENEROUS and the scaling must give ample room to validate complex ACs. We optimize against runaway, never to artificially limit authorized validation.

## Current mechanics (completion.py)
`verify_step_floor(c) = clamp(steps_per_criterion x c, step_floor_min, 480)` with defaults 8/48; structured_run halves steps into pydantic-ai request_limit. A 6-AC epic gets the floor: 48 steps = 24 requests. Defects vs intent:
1. Story-calibrated cost model: 8 steps/criterion assumes repo-file evidence; epic criteria traverse child tickets (show_ticket + comments + repo reads, 5-10 requests each) plus fixed overhead (initial show_ticket, description parse). No evidence-surface term.
2. Runaway is ALREADY separately guarded (tool_calls_limit in-turn backstop, run_failure loop/repeat detection, the 480 clamp), so a small budget adds no safety — only false FAILs.
3. No cross-run carryover: every re-verify re-proves all criteria from scratch (whack-a-mole loops, ~10 min each).

## Plan
1. Raise defaults: completion_verify_steps_per_criterion 8 -> 24, completion_verify_step_floor_min 48 -> 160 (matches the interim user-config mitigation deployed on the operator machine, which this change supersedes). Reconsider the 480 clamp: raise to 960 so 24/criterion scales usefully past 20 ACs — the clamp is a runaway ceiling, not a validation cap.
2. Evidence-surface-aware scaling: budget = per_criterion x c + child_traversal x direct_children (epics/parents) + fixed_overhead. Children counted from the ticket graph at budget-sizing time (same place criteria_count is computed).
3. Cross-run criterion-bank persistence: persist the CriterionBank keyed by (ticket, criterion-text hash, HEAD tree hash / --ref tree); a re-verify credits still-valid banked PASS verdicts without re-proving, invalidating entries when the tree or criterion text changed. Exhaustion then converges across runs instead of whack-a-mole. (Marker semantics from 1d71-a76c-04f6-4642 apply: banked insufficiency stays evidence_sufficient:false, never met=false.)
4. Keep runaway guards authoritative: tool_calls_limit + loop detection unchanged; document in completion.py that the budget exists ONLY for runaway prevention.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Defaults raised (24 / 160; clamp 960) with the rationale documented at verify_step_floor; a 6-AC epic sizes to >=80 requests and a 15-AC epic to >=180; unit tests on the formula.
- [ ] Budget sizing adds a child-traversal term for tickets with direct children, tested with an epic fixture (childful ticket sizes strictly larger than a childless one at equal criteria count).
- [ ] A re-verify after budget exhaustion reuses still-valid banked criterion verdicts (same tree, same criterion text) and only spends budget on unproven criteria; invalidation on tree/text change is tested RED->GREEN.
- [ ] Runaway protection regression-guarded: tool_calls_limit and loop detection behavior unchanged (existing tests still pass); a looping-tool fixture still trips the backstop under the larger budget.
- [ ] `make lint`/`make typecheck` clean; lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1).
data.title: Completion-verifier budget: generous runaway-only floor, evidence-surface scaling, cross-run bank persistence
